Theme

Latin word

intrō

intrō, intrāre, intrāvī, intrātum

verb, first conjugation

go in, come in, enter; in, inside (with verbs of motion); go into, enter

In this lexicon

  • enter

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. 5.9.2: cum vix intrāre posset ad praesēpia; Cic. Phil. 2.68: tū illud sānctissimum līmen intrāre? (Lewis & Short); Traupman 310: enter, intrāre

  • enter

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1387: quīn intrō īs?; Plaut. Aul. 89: abī intrō

  • into

    also used · classical · Vulg. Lc. 10.5: In quamcumque domum intrāveritis

Examples

  • Quis hīc loquitur? ehem, tūne hīc erās, mī Phaedria? Quid hīc stābās? cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?

    who’s that talking? Oh, is it you, Phaedria dear? Why were you standing out here? Why didn’t you come straight in?Ter. Eun. 86–87

    In the entry for enter

  • quid stās? quīn intrō īs?

    why are you standing there? Go on in!Plaut. Mil. 1387
